name: Hibernal-Polje
description: The crust never rests here. Rivers of incandescent basalt vein the lowlands, ash climbs from vents along every fault, and beyond an ancient meteor crater the sky stays the color of a bruise.
In the calm seasons the world feels almost kind, which veterans say is exactly when it takes the careless.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
For traders, geothermal energy, copper and titanium alone justifies the crossing; for everyone else, the planet pays in questions. Fuel is cheap, information is not, and both are dangerous to carry.
